CONTENT HIGHLIGHTS
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Architecture:
  • Pre-forked worker model
  • Event-driven I/O with epoll/kqueue/select
  • Pool-based memory management
  • Accept mutex for thundering herd prevention
  • Zero intra-worker locking
  • HTTP/1.1 request parsing state machine

Concurrency:
  • Shared memory: accept mutex + atomic counters only
  • Connection ownership isolation (per-worker)
  • Cache-line alignment to prevent false sharing
  • NUMA considerations documented
  • Data race analysis

Security:
  • Buffer overflow scenarios and protections
  • 5+ attack patterns (Slowloris, header bomb, request smuggling)
  • Resource exhaustion defense analysis
  • Secure configuration recommendations
  • Testing procedures

Performance:
  • 4 hot paths identified with measurements
  • Cache behavior analysis (L1/L2/L3)
  • Lock contention analysis
  • Tuning checklist (network, connection, memory, OS)
  • Benchmarking methodology

Operations:
  • Pre-deployment validation checklist
  • Ongoing monitoring checklist
  • Incident response procedures
  • Key metrics and alert thresholds
  • Debugging instrumentation points

USAGE BY ROLE
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Backend Engineer (New to nginx):
  Week 1: ARCHITECTURE.md + MEMORY_AND_CONCURRENCY.md (90 min)
  Week 2: CODE_WALKTHROUGH_EVENT_LOOP.md while reading source (2-3 hours)
  → Ready to: understand bugs, optimize performance, navigate codebase

Security Engineer:
  Study: BUFFER_MANAGEMENT.md + ASSUMPTIONS_AND_THREATS.md (2-3 hours)
  Validate: Run security checklist; verify assumptions
  → Verify: System meets security requirements

Performance Engineer:
  Study: PERFORMANCE_BOTTLENECKS.md (30 min)
  Benchmark: Load test procedures (1-2 hours)
  Tune: Apply configuration checklist
  → Maximize: Throughput and efficiency

Operations/SRE:
  Study: README.md → select your path (15 min)
  Validate: Pre-deployment checklist (1-2 hours)
  Monitor: Track ongoing metrics (15 min/week)
  → Ensure: Stability, visibility, resilience

Architect/Principal:
  Study: All documents with critical eye (4-5 hours)
  Challenge: Every assumption; validate trade-offs
  → Verify: Design soundness for your requirements

VALIDATION & DEPLOYMENT
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Pre-Deployment Checklist (from ASSUMPTIONS_AND_THREATS.md):
  ✓ Kernel version (no epoll bugs)
  ✓ NTP synchronized (clock monotonic)
  ✓ Memory available for workload
  ✓ OOM killer configuration
  ✓ File descriptor limits
  ✓ Network tuning (TCP settings)
  ✓ Configuration validated (nginx -t)
  ✓ Modules audited (thread-safety)
  ✓ Storage tuned (local, not NFS)

Ongoing Monitoring:
  ✓ Active connections < 90% of limit
  ✓ Memory stable (not growing)
  ✓ Worker CPU balanced
  ✓ No timeout spikes
  ✓ Cache hit rates > 90%
  ✓ OOM killer never triggered

  • Event modules: ngx_epoll_module.c, ngx_kqueue_module.c
  • Connection: ngx_connection.c, ngx_connection.h

TOOLS & COMMANDS
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Profiling:
  perf record -p $(pgrep nginx) -g
  perf report

Tracing:
  strace -p $(pgrep nginx) -e epoll_wait

Memory Analysis:
  valgrind --leak-check=full nginx

Load Testing:
  ab -n 10000 -c 100 -k http://localhost/
  wrk -t8 -c100 -d30s http://localhost/

System Monitoring:
  watch -n 1 'ps aux | grep nginx'
  ss -tan | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l

CRITICAL ASSUMPTIONS DOCUMENTED
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

1. Event multiplexor is correct (epoll/kqueue/select) [CRITICAL]
2. Clock source is monotonic [HIGH]
3. File descriptors don't wrap [MEDIUM, theoretical]
4. Signals are async-signal-safe [LOW, well-validated]
5. Accept queue doesn't overflow [MEDIUM]
6. Memory allocations never fail silently (OOM) [CRITICAL]
7. Connection pool size matches usage [MEDIUM]
8. Keep-alive timeout works [MEDIUM]
9. epoll/kqueue doesn't lose events [MEDIUM]
10. NUMA cache coherency is sufficient [MEDIUM]
11. Disk I/O is non-blocking [HIGH]
12. Modules don't introduce races [CRITICAL]
13. Configuration syntax validated [MEDIUM]
14. Workers exit cleanly [MEDIUM]
15. Configured limits prevent exhaustion [HIGH]

→ See ASSUMPTIONS_AND_THREATS.md for full analysis
